blurb: If you've got a metalcore fan in the house, Sunday night at the Roxy is calling. Beartooth is one of the harder-hitting acts on the scene right now, and the Coca-Cola Roxy is a great room for this kind of show. It's a solid post-Thanksgiving Sunday night option for anyone in the household who would rather spend the evening in the pit than on the couch. Tickets are available now, but the Roxy sells out, so don't sit on it.
scoring_notes: Metalcore is a narrower niche within the East Cobb demographic, which skews older and more mainstream. However, the mix of established families with teens and college-age kids means there's a real subset who would be interested. Included as the most distinct adult/teen-skewing alternative in the lineup. Lower audience match reflects the niche genre, not a bad event.

blurb: Cap off the holiday week at Depot Park in Downtown Kennesaw on Wednesday evening. The city's Annual Tree Lighting Ceremony kicks off around 6 PM with a choir performance before the main event: lighting the Christmas tree. Hot chocolate is provided by 1885 Grill, which is the kind of detail that actually matters when you're standing outside in December. It's a free, low-key, genuinely warm community night and a solid way to start December on the right foot. Bring the family, grab a cup, and enjoy the kind of neighborhood moment that doesn't cost anything but stays with you.
scoring_notes: Kennesaw is within East Cobb's orbit. Free community event fits the audience's civic-minded, family-oriented character. Hot chocolate detail from a named local restaurant adds a nice specificity. Wednesday night limits the spontaneous turnout factor. Annual recurring event, but tree lighting ceremonies are inherently seasonal and this one opens the December calendar nicely.

event_name: The Nutcracker — Georgia Metropolitan Dance Theatre
blurb: If you want to keep the Nutcracker tradition close to home this Thanksgiving weekend, Georgia Metropolitan Dance Theatre is bringing it right to Marietta. The Jennie T. Anderson Theatre is an easy drive from anywhere in East Cobb, and there's something to be said for supporting a local production over a bigger-venue option. This is a Thanksgiving weekend classic done locally, which makes it easy to work into a holiday weekend without a big commitment on parking or distance. Grab tickets for the family, make an afternoon of it, and check the Nutcracker box before December even gets rolling.
scoring_notes: Jennie T. Anderson Theatre is very close to East Cobb. Competing with the Roswell Dance Theatre Nutcracker reduces its uniqueness score since both are on the same weekend. Local community production angle is a mild differentiator. Good fallback option for families who want something nearby. Scored lower on uniqueness because there are two Nutcracker productions in this same window.

event_name: Sound of Music Sing-A-Long at The Strand
venue: Earl and Rachel Smith Strand Theatre, Marietta
blurb: Sunday afternoon, Marietta's Strand Theatre is turning one of the greatest movie musicals ever made into a full audience participation experience. The Sound of Music Sing-A-Long is exactly what it sounds like: you show up, you sing, nobody judges you, and everyone leaves a little happier than when they walked in. Before the film even starts, there's a live pre-show concert on the Mighty Allen Theatre Organ, which is a rare treat on its own. It's nearly three hours of Do-Re-Mi, Edelweiss, and My Favorite Things sung collectively by a room full of people who definitely know all the words. For the right crowd, this is a PERFECT low-key Sunday with family in town. Grab tickets before they're gone.
scoring_notes: The Strand is local to East Cobb's coverage area. Sing-A-Long format is not something you can do every weekend, adding genuine uniqueness. The 42-year median age skews toward an audience that grew up with this film. Live organ pre-show adds extra value. Slightly more adult-leaning than family, but still broadly appealing for Thanksgiving weekend.

event_name: Roswell Dance Theatre presents The Nutcracker
venue: Sandy Springs Performing Arts Center, Sandy Springs
blurb: If The Nutcracker is part of your family's holiday playbook, Roswell Dance Theatre's production at the Sandy Springs Performing Arts Center is the one to see this weekend. It's a full-scale production with professional dancers, company students, and a cast drawn from the Tolbert Yilmaz School of Dance, running through December 6 with ten total shows. This Saturday's performances are Meet & Greet shows, which means after the curtain comes down, kids can get photos and autographs with the characters. There's also a Nutcracker gift boutique on-site if you want to send someone home with a souvenir. For families with younger kids or grandkids visiting for Thanksgiving, this is a genuinely special afternoon out.
scoring_notes: Sandy Springs is in East Cobb's backyard. The Nutcracker is a cultural staple for the $118K household demographic. Meet & Greet shows this weekend add a unique layer beyond a standard performance. Multi-generational appeal fits the established families and empty-nesters-with-grandkids dynamic well. Multi-show run reduces uniqueness slightly but the holiday weekend timing boosts relevance.

blurb: The holiday season officially kicks off at The Battery Atlanta this Saturday, and it's worth making the trip over. The Tree Lighting brings live entertainment, special guest appearances, and Santa himself showing up to flip the switch on the big tree. Once the lights are on, families spread out on the green for an outdoor movie on the plaza screen. It's a genuinely fun evening with zero barrier to entry, and The Battery does this kind of thing well. If you've got family in town for Thanksgiving weekend, this is a no-brainer way to get everyone off the couch and into the holiday spirit without anyone having to drive far or spend much.
scoring_notes: Thanksgiving weekend timing means family is likely in town, boosting the appeal of a family-friendly free event. The Battery Atlanta is familiar and trusted by East Cobb residents. Free admission removes any friction. Outdoor movie after the lighting adds a second reason to stay. Annual event but the specific date makes it a one-night seasonal moment.

event_name: BLOOPER's Holiday Clubhouse Experience at Truist Park
blurb: This one is genuinely cool, especially if you've got Braves fans in the house over Thanksgiving weekend. BLOOPER's Holiday Clubhouse Experience takes you behind the scenes at Truist Park in a way most fans never get to see: the actual Braves clubhouse, batting cages, dugout access, and the chance to play catch on the field (weather permitting). The whole experience covers up to six guests and includes a holiday photo with BLOOPER Claus, plus a photo op with the 2026 NL East Pennant. If you've got teens who are diehard fans, or if you're just looking for something to do with visiting family that isn't another restaurant reservation, this is the kind of thing people actually remember. It's a Braves-country neighborhood for a reason.
scoring_notes: Truist Park is essentially East Cobb's backyard. Behind-the-scenes access is genuinely rare and can't-miss. Thanksgiving weekend family visit dynamic makes it highly timely. The $118K income demo won't blink at ticket prices. Appeals to teens and adults equally, fitting the older-kids-and-empty-nesters audience well. The 2026 NL East Pennant detail adds a local pride hook.

blurb: Before the turkey hits the table, lace up and head to Marietta Square for one of the most beloved Thanksgiving morning traditions in the area. The Gobble Jog draws over 10,000 runners every year and benefits MUST Ministries, which means every step you take is putting food on someone else's table. There are options for literally everyone: a timed 10K and 5K for the competitive crowd, an untimed 5K for those who just want to move, a 1K, and even a Tot Trot for the little ones. The whole thing has a giant community feel, with area schools, churches, and companies showing up together and nearly 300 volunteers keeping it all moving. It's the kind of Thanksgiving morning that makes the couch feel earned.
scoring_notes: Thanksgiving-morning timing makes this uniquely relevant for this specific issue. 10,000+ attendees signals deep community roots. Multi-distance format fits East Cobb's mix of fitness-minded families and empty nesters perfectly. Charity angle (MUST Ministries) resonates with the educated, civic-minded demographic. Recurring annual event but Thanksgiving-specific, so it qualifies as seasonally unique.
